podcast.body: Costello's seventh album, "Punch the Clock," yielded his only significant North American hit, the Top 40 single "Every Day I Write the Book." By this time, he was often working as a solo artist in the studio, reserving The Attractions primarily for live performances. "Punch the Clock from 1983."

podcast.body: On this album, Costello collaborated with 80s hitmakers Clive Langer and Alan Winstanley, known for their work with MTV staples Madness and Dexys Midnight Runners, signaling his readiness to record more commercially viable songs. The album was influenced by Nick Lowe's "When I Write The Book" and featured the single "Every Day I Write The Book," which significantly boosted Costello's album sales, becoming his best in over three years. The album helped Costello become "conversant" with MTV and re-upholstered his image for the synth pop era. "it fueled punch the clock to Elvis Costello's best album sales in more than three years."
